scope: R7 was the target of this round and IS NOT PROVED. R0 remains open and so does the general codimension-m coarea formula. What is proved is two parts of R7: the local package assembling R2, R3 and R4 into one neighbourhood with a single tangential Lipschitz constant, and the integral form of the target splitting. The remaining gap is stated precisely as R7b and R7c in a check-only file where nothing is proved. NO coarea formula, NO slicing statement about the critical set and NO Sard theorem is proved. No hole migrated. The log-concave Cheeger-Buser line belongs to collaborator Wang Haocheng and was not touched.

existing_lean_modified.status_before: this session's own R4 module, uncommitted
existing_lean_modified.change: refactored so the EXPLICIT constant comes first as lipschitzOnWith_of_ker_bound; the route's existential statement exists_lipschitzOnWith_of_ker_bound is kept VERBATIM and re-derived from it
existing_lean_modified.why_necessary: the assembly needs ONE constant valid on every piece of the approximating partition, and the existential form's constant depends on each piece's linear model, so no uniform bound can be extracted from it

what_is_proved.local_package: exists_stratum_local_data: at a point of the rank-r stratum, with K the range of the differential there and P, Q the orthogonal projections onto K and its complement, there is an open neighbourhood with compact closure on which P composed with u is a submersion, together with ONE constant c that works for EVERY stratum point y in it, every epsilon, every set epsilon-approximated by the differential at y, and every fibre: Q composed with u is c-epsilon-Lipschitz along each fibre of P composed with u
what_is_proved.why_the_uniformity_is_the_difficulty: the approximating partition produces a different linear model on every piece and R4's constant depends on that model through the norm of the differential and the right-inverse bound; the uniform constant comes from R2, the LOCALLY UNIFORM half of R3, and a bound on the norm of the differential near the point - this is where the previous round's insistence on the uniform half of R3 pays off
what_is_proved.target_split: lintegral_split_target: an integral over the target equals the iterated integral over an orthogonal splitting of it, by LinearIsometryEquiv.measurePreserving, WithLp.volume_preserving_toLp and Tonelli, assuming only almost everywhere measurability of the integrand. This is the integral form of what R6 does for null sets, in the shape the per-scale estimate must be integrated against
what_is_proved.supporting: fderiv_clm_comp (chain rule for a continuous linear postcomposition), surjective_proj_comp (the regular component really is a submersion at the base point), finrank_tangentRange_eq (equal dimensions along the stratum)

what_is_missing.contains: 2 #checks and no declaration; NOTHING THERE IS PROVED
what_is_missing.R7b: the per-scale bound: at a fixed epsilon the total fibre measure of the stratum piece over the whole target is at most a constant INDEPENDENT OF EPSILON times epsilon to the power (m - r) times the integral of the coarea Jacobian of the regular component
what_is_missing.R7b_route: run the approximating partition on u ITSELF so one partition serves both components; use the local package on each piece; apply the Eilenberg bound INSIDE a fibre at exponent k with a target of dimension m - r, where k + (m - r) = n - r is exactly right; integrate over the fibre parameter against the PROVED regular coarea formula, which converts fibre measures into an ordinary integral of the coarea Jacobian; read the result through lintegral_split_target
what_is_missing.R7c: the limit epsilon to zero, which is the pattern already used twice in the repository, in VectorHausdorffSlicing.lean and VectorCriticalSlice.lean
what_is_missing.consequence: until both are proved, R7 is open, and with it R0 and the general codimension-m coarea formula
